card: This pull request encapsulates HTTP request parsing state by removing HTTPRequest::SetState(), making per-section parsing methods private, and introducing a single HTTPRequest::Load() method that advances internal state automatically. It resolves an encapsulation leak highlighted during review of PR 35829, where external callers could still manipulate the request state enum. Additionally, HTTPRemoteClient::ReadRequest() is flattened into an internal member method. There are no behavioral changes or prerequisites.
changed_since_previous: Rebased with minor adjustments; the overall approach and commit structure remain unchanged.
evidence: Author cites a review discussion on PR 35829 pointing out that external callers could still mutate request state enum directly: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35829#discussion_r3860447518
problem: After PR 35829 made HTTPRequest fields private, any caller holding a reference to a request could still arbitrarily overwrite its internal state enum via SetState(). Callers also had to orchestrate the sequential parsing steps for control data, headers, and body manually.

risk.why: A parsing logic or state progression bug in the HTTP server could reject valid RPC requests or crash the RPC server thread.

summary: Encapsulates HTTP request state transitions by removing HTTPRequest::SetState() and making individual parsing functions private. A unified HTTPRequest::Load() method now drives the parsing pipeline and updates internal state directly. Additionally, request parsing in HTTPRemoteClient is flattened from ReadRequest() into a private TryReadRequestInternal() member function.
